reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Probability.predictableSigma
Standing setting (paper section 2, intro (eq:mvfbsdej), section 3 solution space, section 4,
appendix A): (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0; a d-dim
Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity
dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, calE); (F_t) is the usual augmentation
of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0. The compensated
measure is Ntilde(dt,de) = N(dt,de) - dt nu(de). Integrands U of the Poisson integral are
predictable: P (x) calE-measurable, P the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]
(eq:fubiniiso), with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L2(nu)} dt < infinity (the space H^2_N). The
integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) is the standard L2 (Ito-Levy) compensated-Poisson
integral: an L2 martingale, cadlag, with the isometry E|int_0^t int U dNtilde|^2 =
E int_0^t ||U_s||^2 ds (used in Lemma 4.1 "true L2-martingales by the Ito and
compensated-Poisson isometries"), jumps Delta = U_s(e) at atoms (s,e) of N, and for integrands
in L1(dP dt nu) the integral splits as int U dN - int U nu ds (eq:compid, eq:zeromean).
Progressive measurability is used for the coefficient processes b, sigma, f and the forcings
q^b, q^sigma, q^f (eq:coefmeas, section 4); predictability (P (x) calE) for h and q^h.

Reading.
Paper notion: "P := predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]" (eq:fubiniiso), relative to the
filtration (F_t) of the setting. Standard definition: the sigma-algebra on (time) x Omega
generated by the left-continuous adapted processes; equivalently generated by the predictable
rectangles (s,t] x A, s < t, A in F_s, together with {0} x A, A in F_0. Faithful Lean: the
sigma-algebra generated by those rectangles for the given filtration (time domain [0,infinity)
or [0,T]; either order of the factors). Representation choices: dropping the {0} x A generators
changes only the time-0 slice (predictable processes then have an omega-constant time-0 value),
harmless for all uses under dt x dP (the paper's predictability is used only for the integrands
Z, U and h, q^h, which matter only dt x dP-a.e.), but not harmless for a statement that a
process with a random time-0 value is predictable. Generators with closed left endpoint
[s,t] x A, A in F_s, would be wrong ({s} x A with A in F_s is not predictable in general). The
sigma-algebra must be contained in (Borel time) (x) (ambient sigma-algebra).

comparison.text:
Lean (LevyStochCalc/Probability/Predictable.lean): predictableSigma F : MeasurableSpace (R x Omega)
:= generateFrom ({Iic 0 x A : A in F 0} union {Ioi r x A : r in R, A in F r}).
Comparison with the locked reading:
 - generators (r, inf) x A with A in F r instead of (s,t] x A with A in F s: the same
   sigma-algebra ((s,t] x A = (s,inf) x A minus (t,inf) x A with A in F s <= F t; conversely
   (s,inf) x A is the countable union of (s,s+n] x A);
 - initial cell: (-inf,0] x A with A in F 0, whose trace on [0,inf) x Omega is the standard
   {0} x A, A in F_0 (so the time-0 slice is the standard one - no loss of random time-0
   values);
 - trace on [0,inf) x Omega: generators with r < 0 give [0,inf) x A, A in F r <= F 0, which is
   {0} x A union (0,inf) x A, already standard; so the trace is exactly the standard predictable
   sigma-field of the filtration on [0,inf), and restricting further to [0,T] x Omega gives the
   paper's P;
 - open left endpoints (correct, no closed-left generators);
 - contained in Borel(R) (x) m0 (generators are measurable rectangles).
Representation choices: time axis R with the convention (stated in the module doc) that the
filtration is constant on (-inf,0]; under that convention the initial cell is redundant, and in
any case the behaviour at negative times has no paper counterpart. Order R x Omega. Harmless.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices: (1) time axis R, with the module's convention that the filtration is
constant on (-inf,0]; (2) generators (r,inf) x A (A in F r) instead of (s,t] x A - the same
sigma-algebra; (3) the initial cell (-inf,0] x A, A in F 0, whose trace on [0,inf) x Omega is the
standard {0} x A; the trace of predictableSigma on [0,T] x Omega is exactly the paper's
predictable sigma-field P; behaviour at negative times has no paper counterpart.
